title: Predicting the Filipino Household Income Using Naive Bayes Classification Algorithm
authors: Apus, J.O.; Mantalaba, K.D.V.; Mackno, A.J.B.; Bokingkito, P.B.
venue: International Journal of Computing and Digital Systems
tldr: Naive Bayes with bagging ensemble achieved 93% accuracy predicting Filipino income classes from household expenditure and income features using FIES data.
problem_and_motivation: Predicting Filipino economic class has relied on socio-demographic variables like age and occupation, leaving household expenditure and income variables underexplored as predictive features. Accurate income classification from spending data could help local government units target poverty reduction programs to vulnerable households.
approach: Used the 2018 FIES dataset from the Philippine Statistics Authority containing 41,545 household instances and 60 features.
Applied data cleaning: replaced missing values using mode for categorical and mean/median for numeric attributes.
Performed univariate chi-squared feature selection via SelectKBest, retaining 13 features with highest scores from the original 60.
Implemented Naive Bayes classifier with two ensemble techniques: bagging and boosting.
Split data 80-20 into training and testing sets following the Pareto Principle.
Evaluated models using confusion matrix, accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics.
findings: Bagging Naive Bayes (Model I) achieved 93% accuracy with precision 0.93, recall 0.94, and F1-score 0.94.
Boosting Naive Bayes (Model II) achieved 89% accuracy with precision 0.90, recall 0.93, and F1-score 0.91.
Total Food Expenditure yielded the highest chi-squared feature selection score of 7.23, making it the most discriminative predictor.
Transportation Expenditure scored 5.54 and Total Income from Entrepreneurial Activities scored 5.46 as top predictive features.
The FIES dataset contained 41,545 household instances across 60 original features before selection.
13 features were retained after chi-squared feature selection from the original 60 features.
Poor income class yielded the most true positives while Rich class had the fewest for both models.
Both ensemble models exceeded the 80% accuracy threshold considered acceptable in scientific literature.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a Naive Bayes classifier for predicting Filipino household income classes using expenditure and income variables from the FIES dataset, rather than relying on socio-demographic features. It demonstrates that ensemble bagging with Naive Bayes achieves 93% accuracy on a seven-class income classification problem.
directly_justifies: Naive Bayes with bagging ensemble achieved 93% accuracy predicting Filipino income classes from expenditure data.
Total Food Expenditure yielded the highest chi-squared score of 7.23 among 60 features for income class prediction.
Prior studies used socio-demographic variables; this study demonstrates expenditure and income variables as effective features.
Thirteen expenditure and income features were selected from sixty using univariate chi-squared statistical tests.
Boosting Naive Bayes achieved 89% accuracy, also exceeding the acceptable 80% threshold for classification models.
limits: Study uses only one dataset (2018 FIES) without cross-validation across multiple survey waves.
Naive Bayes assumes feature independence, which may not hold for correlated expenditure categories.
No comparison with other classifiers such as decision trees, SVMs, or neural networks on the same features.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 1 was flagged at low relevance because the paper studies Filipino households generally. Domain 2 received medium relevance due to Philippine-specific income brackets and Special Occasions Expenditure. Domain 3 received medium relevance as the paper selects and uses 13 expenditure categories. Domain 5 received high relevance for its core classification methodology. Domain 6 received high relevance as the paper's primary contribution. All other domains were considered and rejected.

limitations: Study uses only one FIES dataset without cross-validation across multiple survey waves. [unacknowledged]
Naive Bayes assumes feature independence, which may not hold for correlated expenditure categories. [unacknowledged]
No comparison with other classifiers such as decision trees, random forests, or neural networks on the same feature set.
Feature selection using chi-squared may miss non-linear relationships between expenditure variables and income class.
remember_this: Bagging Naive Bayes achieved 93% accuracy on seven-class Filipino income prediction from FIES expenditure data.
Total Food Expenditure was the strongest predictor with a chi-squared score of 7.23 among 60 features.
Thirteen expenditure and income features outperformed socio-demographic variables for income class classification.
Boosting Naive Bayes achieved 89% accuracy, also exceeding the acceptable 80% threshold for good models.
